newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's FEMSA raises beer prices 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's FEMSA raises beer prices 22 pct.

text.p: Mexico's No. 2 brewer Cerveceria Cuauhtemoc Moctezuma, owned by Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV (FEMSA), on Monday said it raised beer prices to retailers by 22 percent.

"Cerveceria Cuauhtemoc Moctezuma announced today that it has taken all the steps necessary to increase the price of beer to retailers by a national average of 22 percent effective this date (February 24)," the company said in news release.

Should Mexican consumer prices this year rise by about 18 percent, as many economists predict, the increase announced by FEMSA would mark the first real rise in prices charged by the company in several years.
The company said price increases of 26 percent in 1996 and 24 percent in 1995 have lagged inflation in those years. Mexican inflation reached 27.7 percent in 1996 and 52 percent the previous year.
The 22 percent rise in prices is slightly higher than predicted by beer analysts, who expected the increase to be line with the inflation forecasts of about 18 percent.
FEMSA makes Tecate, Carta Blanca, Superior, Sol, Dos Equis and Bohemia, among other brands.
